about.title: Anderson Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Anderson sits along a stretch of Shasta County where Rt 273, I-5, Deschutes Road, and North Street carry a steady flow of local and through traffic. Public records show 26 injury collisions and 40 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with a single traffic death, and reports tend to cluster on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memories fade quickly. We handle personal injury claims for Anderson residents injured in car accidents. Our team can evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and explain your options under California law. There's no cost for your free consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning we're paid only if you recover compensation. You focus on healing; let us handle the calls.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but if a government entity (like a road authority) may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for the crash, you may still recover a reduced share of damages. Insurers often try to shift blame early, sometimes through a recorded statement, so it helps to have someone protecting your side of the story.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers won't hand that value over easily. Working on contingency, we have an incentive to pursue full value since we're only paid if you recover.

items.question: What should I do after a crash on Rt 273 or Deschutes Road?
items.answer: Seek medical care first, even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up later. Try to document the scene with photos if you're able, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer until you've spoken with an attorney. Rt 273 and Deschutes Road see regular traffic, so witness accounts and any available footage can matter.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Your free consultation is at no cost, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.

items.question: Is there really a shorter deadline if a government road or agency is involved?
items.answer: Yes. While California generally gives you two years to file a personal injury lawsuit, claims involving a government entity, such as a public roadway defect, often require a formal claim within six months. Given that Anderson's crash reports involve corridors like I-5 and North Street, it's worth checking this quickly.
